title: 7.3 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can go beyond today's lesson: solve one-step multiplication and division equations using inverse operations in trickier cases, and explain WHY it works.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: Detective Park lines up 3 identical locked evidence boxes on a table. Together the 3 boxes hold 21 pieces of evidence, and each box holds the same amount. She writes 3x = 21 to find how many pieces are in each box.
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Evidence Boxes
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Park splits 96 pieces of evidence equally among several identical boxes. Each box ends up holding exactly 8 pieces. The equation 8b = 96 represents this situation, where b is the number of boxes. How many boxes did she use? Show your work using inverse operations.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Divide both sides of 8b = 96 by 8: b = 96 ÷ 8 = 12 boxes. Check: 8 × 12 = 96. ✓

turnAndTalk.question: Detective Park has 3 identical boxes holding 21 pieces of evidence total, written as 3x = 21. What does each part of the equation mean, and how is solving this different from solving x + 3 = 21?
turnAndTalk.kernel: In 3x = 21 the variable is multiplied, so I undo it with division.

stems.en: Solving 3x = 21 is different from x + 3 = 21 because ___.
stems.es: Resolver 3x = 21 es diferente de x + 3 = 21 porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Predict: would x in 3x = 21 be larger or smaller than in 5x = 21? Justify before solving.
extendStems: More boxes means each box has ___.

turnAndTalk.question: How did you undo the multiplication in 3x = 21 (or the division in x / 4 = 9) to isolate the variable?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I use the inverse operation: division undoes multiplication.

stems.en: I divided / multiplied both sides by ___, so the answer is ___.
stems.es: Dividí / multipliqué ambos lados por ___, así que la respuesta es ___.

stems.en: The inverse of ___ is ___, so I ___.
stems.es: El inverso de ___ es ___, así que ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Why does dividing only one side of 3x = 21 give the wrong answer? Compare doing it to one side versus both sides.
extendStems: Dividing only one side is wrong because ___.
To keep the equation true I must ___.

turnAndTalk.question: When would you solve a multiplication or division equation in real life?
turnAndTalk.kernel: These equations find an unknown when items are split into or made from equal groups.

stems.en: I would use this kind of equation to find ___.
stems.es: Usaría este tipo de ecuación para hallar ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Critique: 'To solve x / 5 = 12 you divide both sides by 5.' Explain the error and the correct inverse operation.
extendStems: This is wrong because the inverse of division is ___.
I should ___ both sides by 5, which gives ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Solve Multiplication and Division Equations, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

stems.en: I divided / multiplied both sides by ___, so the answer is ___.
stems.es: Dividí / multipliqué ambos lados por ___, así que la respuesta es ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate multiplied again instead of dividing to solve 6x = 42 (and got x = 252). How would you help them fix this common mistake? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two math actions that undo each other, like × and ÷.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos operaciones que se deshacen entre sí, como × y ÷.
vocabulary.visual: Multiplication and division are inverses: 3 × 7 = 21, so 21 ÷ 3 = 7
vocabulary.cloze: An operation that undoes another, like division undoing multiplication, is an ___.

examples.text: Dividing by 4 to undo multiplying by 4
Multiplying by 4 to undo multiplying by 4
examples.why: Multiplying again does not undo it.

vocabulary.definition: To add equal groups again and again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar grupos iguales una y otra vez.
vocabulary.cloze: To undo dividing by a number, I ___ both sides by that number.

vocabulary.visual: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 means 36 split into 4 equal groups gives 9 per group
vocabulary.cloze: To undo multiplying by a number, I ___ both sides by that number.

vocabulary.definition: To get the letter by itself on one side.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dejar la letra sola en un lado.
vocabulary.visual: 3x = 21 → divide both sides by 3 → x = 7 (x is alone)
vocabulary.cloze: To get the variable alone on one side is to ___ it.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I solve a multiplication or division equation?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Solve 3x = 21. This means 3 times x equals 21.
The inverse of multiplying by 3 is dividing by 3.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Solve each equation by showing your work. Use inverse operations to isolate the variable. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.
hints: For multiplication equations like 3x = 21, the inverse is division. Divide both sides by the coefficient.
For division equations like x / 4 = 9, the inverse is multiplication. Multiply both sides by the divisor.
explore.label: Complete the table to solve each equation. Show your inverse operation and work.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide to solve an equation?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I see ___ in the equation, I know to ___ both sides because the inverse of ___ is ___.

onLevel.stem: A detective splits 54 clues equally among 9 case files. The equation 9c = 54 represents this. What is c?
onLevel.explanation: Divide both sides by 9: c = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 clues per file.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: c is the number of clues in EACH file, and 9 files with c clues each make all 54 clues.
9c = 54 multiplies c by 9 — undo it by dividing both sides by 9, not by adding or subtracting.
Compute 54 ÷ 9 (what times 9 makes 54?). Your answer should be much smaller than 54 — clues per file, not the total.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Choose operation
workedExample.work: n is in a fraction, so I will divide both sides by 4.

onLevel.correctWork: n is divided by 4, so the inverse is MULTIPLICATION. Multiply both sides by 4: n = 12 × 4 = 48. Check: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 ✓
hints: The student divided again instead of multiplying. Division does not undo division.
To undo ÷ 4, you must × 4. Multiply both sides by 4 to isolate n.

onLevel.title: Find the Equation Error
onLevel.correctWork: Inverse of division is MULTIPLICATION. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 12 × 5 = 60. Check: 60 / 5 = 12 ✓
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of division is division. Is that correct?
To undo ÷ 5, you need × 5. Multiplication undoes division.

onLevel.prompt: A bakery packed muffins into boxes of 8. They made 96 muffins total. Write an equation, solve it, and explain why your answer is reasonable. Then write a different situation that uses division and has the same answer.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Equation: ___. Solving: ___. The answer ___ is reasonable because ___. A division situation with the same answer: ___.
onLevel.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: You know the total (96 muffins) and the size of each group (8 per box). The unknown is how many boxes.
Write a multiplication model with 8 and the unknown box count equal to 96, then divide both sides by 8. 'Reasonable' means boxes × 8 rebuilds 96.
Compute 96 ÷ 8 for the number of boxes. For your new story, pick a different total and divisor that give the SAME quotient.

extending.stem: Vault A is sealed with 4x = 32. Crack the lock: what is x?
extending.explanation: The 4 is multiplying x, so divide both sides by 4: x = 32 / 4 = 8. Check: 4 x 8 = 32.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.

extending.stem: Vault B is sealed with x / 3 = 6. Crack the lock: what is x?
extending.explanation: x is divided by 3, so multiply both sides by 3: x = 6 x 3 = 18. Check: 18 / 3 = 6.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.

extending.stem: Vault C is sealed with 5n = 45. Crack the lock: what is n?
extending.explanation: The 5 is multiplying n, so divide both sides by 5: n = 45 / 5 = 9. Check: 5 x 9 = 45.
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension - The Vault That Won't Open
extending.correctWork: The inverse of multiplication is DIVISION. Divide both sides by 4: x = 32 / 4 = 8. Check: 4 x 8 = 32.
hints: Step 2 says to multiply to undo multiplying. Does multiplying again get the variable alone?
To undo x 4, you must / 4. Division unlocks a multiplication equation.

extending.explanation: Divide both sides by 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: 6x means 6 TIMES x — the variable is being multiplied by 6.
Division undoes multiplication. Divide both sides by 6 to leave x alone.
Compute 42 ÷ 6, then check by multiplying your answer by 6 — do you get 42 back?

extending.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Check: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: n is being DIVIDED by 3. Which operation undoes division?
Multiply both sides by 3 — the ÷3 and ×3 cancel each other, leaving just n.
Compute 8 × 3, then check: your answer divided by 3 should give 8.

extending.explanation: Divide both sides by 9: m = 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Check: 9 × 7 = 63 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: 9m means 9 times m — that's multiplication, even with no × symbol written.
Undo the multiplication with division: divide both sides by 9.
Compute 63 ÷ 9 (think: 9 times what equals 63?). Check by multiplying your answer back by 9.

extending.explanation: Multiply both sides by 7: y = 5 × 7 = 35. Check: 35 / 7 = 5 ✓
choiceFeedback: Check your operation. Re-read what the problem asks.
hints: y is split into 7 equal parts. To rebuild y, you need the opposite of dividing.
Multiply both sides by 7 so y stands alone on the left.
Compute 5 × 7, then confirm: your answer ÷ 7 should land back on 5.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Solve Multiplication and Division Equations is applying the SAME operation again instead of the inverse — for example, seeing 6x = 42 and multiplying both sides by 6 to get x = 252, instead of dividing by 6 to get x = 7. Before you submit, ask: did I use the OPPOSITE operation shown in the equation, and did I apply it to both sides?

diagram.title: Splitting the $63 Kit Bill
diagram.caption: The top bar is the whole bill ($63); below it we split it into equal $7 groups — counting the 9 groups shows k = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 kits.

connect.scenario: A detective ordered fingerprint kits for her team. Each kit costs $7, and the total bill was $63. The equation 7k = 63 represents this situation, where k is the number of kits.
connect.promptQuestion: How many kits did the detective order? How did inverse operations help you solve this?
connect.prompt: The detective ordered ___ kits because 7k = 63 means k = 63 ÷ ___ = ___.

exitTicket.explanation: Multiply both sides by 8: w = 6 × 8 = 48. Check: 48 / 8 = 6 ✓
choiceFeedback: You added 8 — undo division by multiplying both sides by 8.
You divided again — multiply 6 by 8 to undo w ÷ 8.
That's 8 − 6 — instead multiply to undo the division.
hints: w is being divided by 8. Name that operation before you touch any numbers.
Multiplication undoes division — multiply both sides by 8 to get w alone. Don't subtract, and don't divide again.
Compute 6 × 8 for w, then check: your w divided by 8 should give exactly 6.
